newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: TENNIS-ENQVIST PUTS SWEDEN INTO DAVIS CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-ENQVIST PUTS SWEDEN INTO DAVIS CUP FINAL.

text.p: Thomas Enqvist won Sweden a place in the Davis Cup final when he fought back from 2-1 down to beat Czech Daniel Vacek in an epic three and a half hour battle on Sunday.
Enqvist took the first reverse singles match 6-3 6-7 4-6 7-5 6-3 to give Sweden an unbeatable 3-1 lead in their world group semifinal.
The Czech Republic had kept their hopes alive by winning Saturday's doubles and Vacek looked to be on the way to squaring the tie when he moved in to a 2-1 lead after losing the first set.

Vacek made the first service break of the match when he took the fifth game in the first set but the Swedish number one immediately returned the favour, breaking back and then surging ahead with another break in Vacek's next service game to take the set 6-3.
Enqvist, who had never faced Vacek before, then opened the second frame with another break and appeared to have the top ranked Czech at his mercy.
But then Enqvist's serve began to fail miserably while Vacek hit his stride, becoming more confident with each shot. He broke back and then overpowered Enqvist in a tie break 7-3.

With a partisan crowd firmly behind him, Vacek continued to press the faltering Enqvist, watching him double fault and then miss an easy volley to give up the break needed to allow the Czech to take the third set 6-4.
The two went toe-to-toe in a hard-hitting fourth set, neither surrendering a break point until the 12th game when the Swede used his blistering returns to break Vacek and win 7-5.

Enqvist who's serve had failed him throughout most of the match as he double faulted 18 times, finally found the rythym in the final set, firing five of his 18 aces to overcome an early break by Vacek with one of his own in the fifth game.
The break proved to be the turning point in the match as Vacek lost his temper, slamming the net twice with his racket and earning a warning from umpire Bruno Rebeuh.
Vacek, who served 27 aces, could not stem the tide, giving up a break in the eighth game and allowing Enqvist to serve out the match, putting six times champions Sweden into the final.
"I was very upset after the break in the fifth set. It was an emotional match, one of the toughest I have ever played. Every point was a battle," Enqvist said.
"I lost my timing on the serve and Daniel was putting a lot of pressure on my second serve. After a while, I began to come in after my serve to mix it up and find my rythym again."
Vacek commented: "I played probably the best game of my career today, it's too bad I couldn't win such an important point for our team.
"I had a chance in the final set with the early break and tried to pressure him but he responded and found his serve."
Victory will give Stefan Edberg, in the final year of his distinguished career, a chance to win his fourth Davis Cup trophy.
Edberg closed out the tie with a 4-6 6-2 7-5 win in a shortened match over his Australian Open doubles championship partner Petr Korda, giving the Swedes a 4-1 overall score.
"It's tough playing after the emotional high of (Enqvist's) win but I think we both played a rather strong match. And now we go back to being friends, just as always," said Edberg.
Sweden will face France in the final after Arnaud Boetsch's straight-sets victory over Italian Andrea Gaudenzi gave the French a 3-2 triumph in the other semifinal in Nantes.
Like the Czechs, France faced elimination after going down 2-0 in the opening singles, but came roaring back to win the three remaining matches.
